messages:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to unify transport + retry surface across Python/TS/Go. TL;DR: one minimal transport interface (sync/async variants) + pluggable RetryPolicy + explicit stream resume tokens for pagination/streaming. Thoughts?

Maya: +1 to unify. Biggest win is reducing per-lang behavioural surprises. Do we require resume_token in every stream event?

Jon: Prefer resume_token as explicit field on stream events (metadata) rather than implicit cursor in headers. That makes client libraries much simpler to reason about when implementing resume.

Priya: Tradeoff note: ergonomics differ per language. Python wants generator/yield, TS wants AsyncIterable, Go typically expects channel/iterator. How much should transport try to model those vs be minimal?

Sam: My suggestion: core transport stays minimal: `send(req) -> resp`, `stream(req) -> StreamHandle`. Language-layer adapters convert StreamHandle -> generator/async-iter/channel. Keep retry concerns separated into a RetryPolicy object that the transport invokes.

Maya: Prototype transport sketch (pseudo):
```
interface RetryPolicy {
  shouldRetry(err, attempt): bool
  nextDelay(attempt): Duration
}

interface Transport {
  send(Request req, RetryPolicy retry): Response
  stream(Request req): StreamHandle // StreamHandle.next() -> Event | EOF
}

struct Event {
  data: bytes
  resume_token?: string
  meta: map[string]string
}
```

Jon: On retries we need two layers: 1) transport-level idempotent retries for unary calls, 2) client-level resume/retry for streaming/pagination using resume_token. Default policy: transport retries only if request marked idempotent. Client libraries implement resume using the token.

Priya: Backoff defaults proposal: exponential + full jitter, base=100ms, cap=5s, max_attempts=5. Make these consistent across languages.

Maya: Also require well-defined error taxonomy: TransientError vs PermanentError vs ResumeableStreamError so languages can map to native error types. Add to RFC.

DevBot: I created branch `rfc/transport-retry-unify` and pushed initial draft: https://github.com/redwood/rfcs/tree/rfc/transport-retry-unify — feel free to push examples.

Sam: @Maya @Priya can you mock minimal Python + TS APIs that adapt the StreamHandle to native iterators? I can take Go after that.

Maya: Will do. Quick Python sketch in head: `for chunk in client.stream(req): process(chunk)` where client.stream wraps StreamHandle and yields (data, resume_token) tuples.

Jon: One open Q: streaming LLM outputs may emit very frequent small messages; resume_token per-event could be too granular. Maybe server emits token every N bytes or per checkpoint.

Priya: Agreed — pragmatic approach: server includes token optionally; client should support both granular tokens and checkpointed tokens. Also expose `seek_to(token)` on StreamHandle for explicit resume.

Maya: TS will expose `for await (const ev of client.stream(req))` and `ev.resumeToken` optional. Also add `stream.seek(token)` API.

Sam: OK, next steps: Maya/Priya prototype adapters for py/ts this week, Jon sketches Go pattern, I update RFC with interface and examples, then sync on Fri eng-platform. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
